import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.2

by V. S. Anashin

A mixed identity of a group is an identity in variables and additional
constant symbols. A class is a mixed variety if there is a fixed set of
constant symbols and mixed identities such that a group belongs to the class
exactly when some interpretation of the constants makes every identity hold.

Construct a class of groups that is not a mixed variety, but is closed under
factor groups, arbitrary Cartesian products, and subgroups of arbitrary
Cartesian powers that contain the diagonal subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.2»

/-- A class of groups in a fixed universe. -/
abbrev GroupClass := GrpCat.{0} → Prop

/-- A class of groups is isomorphism-closed if membership is preserved by
group isomorphisms. -/
def IsIsomorphismClosed (𝒞 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ G H : GrpCat, Nonempty (G ≅ H) → 𝒞 G → 𝒞 H

/-- A class of groups is closed under factor groups if the quotient by every
normal subgroup of a member is again a member. -/
def IsClosedUnderFactorGroups (𝒞 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : GrpCat) (_ : 𝒞 G) (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝒞 (.of (G ⧸ N))

/-- A class of groups is closed under arbitrary Cartesian products. The index
type may be empty. -/
def IsClosedUnderCartesianProducts (𝒞 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ (I : Type) (G : I → GrpCat), (∀ i, 𝒞 (G i)) → 𝒞 (.of (∀ i, G i))

/-- A class has the required Cartesian-power subgroup closure if, for every
member $G$, every subgroup of an arbitrary power $G^I$ that contains all
constant tuples (the diagonal copy of $G$) is again a member. -/
def IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroupsOfPowers (𝒞 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : GrpCat) (_ : 𝒞 G) (I : Type) (H : Subgroup (I → G)),
    (∀ g : G, (fun _ ↦ g) ∈ H) → 𝒞 (.of H)

/-- A mixed variety is specified by constant symbols and group words in those
symbols and countably many variables. A group belongs exactly when there is
an interpretation of the constants under which every word evaluates to the
identity for every assignment of the variables. Writing identities as words
equal to $1$ is equivalent to writing equations between two words. -/
def IsMixedVariety (𝒞 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : Type) (identities : Set (FreeGroup (ℕ ⊕ C))),
    ∀ G : GrpCat, 𝒞 G ↔
      ∃ constants : C → G, ∀ assignment : ℕ → G, ∀ w ∈ identities,
        FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim assignment constants) w = 1

/--
Construct an isomorphism-closed class of groups which is not a mixed variety,
but which is closed under factor groups, arbitrary unrestricted Cartesian
products, and subgroups of arbitrary Cartesian powers that contain the
diagonal subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.2» :
    ∃ 𝒞 : GroupClass,
      IsIsomorphismClosed 𝒞 ∧
      IsClosedUnderFactorGroups 𝒞 ∧
      IsClosedUnderCartesianProducts 𝒞 ∧
      IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroupsOfPowers 𝒞 ∧
      ¬ IsMixedVariety 𝒞 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.2»
modeling_decisions: A class of groups is represented as a predicate on Mathlib's bundled small groups `GrpCat.{0}`; all claims about arbitrary products and signatures are relative to this fixed universe.

Mixed identities are normalized from equations between words to free-group words equal to the identity. They use countably many variable symbols, which is sufficient because each group word is finite, and an arbitrary small type of constant symbols.
Membership in a mixed variety has quantifier order: there exists one interpretation of all constant symbols in the group, then every identity holds under every assignment of the variables.

Containment of the diagonal subgroup in a subgroup of `G^I` is expressed directly by requiring every constant function `I → G` to belong to the subgroup. The index type is unrestricted and may be empty.
Closure under factor groups is represented by canonical quotients by all normal subgroups; the separately required isomorphism closure makes this independent of the chosen quotient presentation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.2

by V. S. Anashin

A *mixed identity* of a group $G$ is, by definition, an identity of an algebraic system
obtained from $G$ by supplementing its signature by some set of $0$-ary operations.
One can develop a theory of mixed varieties of groups on the basis of this notion
(see, for example, V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*,
Math. USSR Sbornik **57** (1987), 171–182). Construct an example of a class of groups
which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed under taking factor-groups, Cartesian
products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the diagonal subgroup.

Here a mixed identity is a word $w$ in variables from a set $X$ and constant symbols from a
set $C$ (the $0$-ary operations), i.e. an element of the free group on $X \sqcup C$. A group
$G$ with an interpretation $c \colon C \to G$ of the constants satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates
to $1$ for all values of the variables in $G$. A class of groups is a *mixed variety* (in
Anashin's sense) if, for some set $W$ of mixed identities, it consists exactly of the groups
in which all identities of $W$ hold for some interpretation of the constants.

Every mixed variety is closed under isomorphism, factor-groups, Cartesian products (over
arbitrary index sets, so it contains the trivial group) and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup. The problem asks for a class showing that these closure
properties do not characterise mixed varieties, in contrast with Birkhoff's theorem for
ordinary varieties.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
* V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*, Math. USSR Sbornik
  **57** (1987), 171–182.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.2»

/-- A group `G` together with an interpretation `c : C → G` of the constant symbols `C`
satisfies the mixed identity `w` (a word in the variables `X` and the constants `C`) if `w`
evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the variables. -/
def SatisfiesMixedIdentity {X C : Type} (G : Type) [Group G] (c : C → G)
    (w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X → G, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c) w = 1

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is a *mixed variety* if there are a set `X` of variables, a set `C`
of constant symbols and a set `W` of mixed identities (words in `X` and `C`) such that a group
belongs to `𝒞` if and only if all identities in `W` hold in it for some interpretation of the
constants. -/
def IsMixedVariety (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X C : Type) (W : Set (FreeGroup (X ⊕ C))),
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒞 G ↔ ∃ c : C → G, ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsClosedUnderIso (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], 𝒞 G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) → 𝒞 H

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking factor-groups. -/
def IsClosedUnderQuotients (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝒞 G → 𝒞 (G ⧸ N)

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets
(including the empty one, whose product is the trivial group). -/
def IsClosedUnderPiProducts (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, 𝒞 (G i)) → 𝒞 (∀ i, G i)

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking those subgroups of Cartesian powers `Gⁱ` of
its members that contain the diagonal subgroup `{(g)ᵢ : g ∈ G}`, i.e. the range of
`Pi.constMonoidHom ι G`. -/
def IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι G : Type) [Group G] (H : Subgroup (ι → G)),
    𝒞 G → (Pi.constMonoidHom ι G).range ≤ H → 𝒞 H

/--
Construct an example of a class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed
under taking factor-groups, Cartesian products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that
contain the diagonal subgroup.

Formally: there is an (isomorphism-closed) class of groups which is closed under
factor-groups, Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup, but which is not a mixed variety.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.2» :
    ∃ 𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop,
      IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 ∧
        IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 ∧ ¬ IsMixedVariety 𝒞 := by
  sorry

/- ### Basic properties of mixed identities and mixed varieties

Every mixed variety has the four closure properties appearing in the problem, so these are
necessary conditions; the problem asks whether they are sufficient. -/

/-- Mixed identities are preserved by surjective homomorphisms. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.map {X C G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (f : G →* H)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (f ∘ c) w := by
  intro y
  choose x hx using fun v => hf (y v)
  have key : f.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c)) = FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim y (f ∘ c)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp [hx]
  simpa [hw x] using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).symm

/-- Mixed identities pass to subgroups containing the constants. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.subgroup {X C G : Type} [Group G] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (H : Subgroup G)
    (hc : ∀ k, c k ∈ H) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩) w := by
  intro x
  have key : H.subtype.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => (x v : G)) c) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw _)

/-- Mixed identities hold componentwise in Cartesian products. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi {X C ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    {c : ∀ i, C → G i} {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)}
    (hw : ∀ i, SatisfiesMixedIdentity (G i) (c i) w) :
    SatisfiesMixedIdentity (∀ i, G i) (fun k i => c i k) w := by
  intro x
  ext i
  have key : (Pi.evalMonoidHom G i).comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k i => c i k)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => x v i) (c i)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw i _)

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderIso {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro G H _ _ hG ⟨e⟩
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨e ∘ c, fun w hw => (hc w hw).map e.toMonoidHom e.surjective⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under taking factor-groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderQuotients {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro G _ N _ hG
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW _).mpr ⟨QuotientGroup.mk' N ∘ c, fun w hw =>
    (hc w hw).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective N)⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under Cartesian products. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderPiProducts {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro ι G _ hG
  choose c hc using fun i => (hW (G i)).mp (hG i)
  exact (hW _).mpr ⟨fun k i => c i k, fun w hw => .pi fun i => hc i w hw⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the
diagonal subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro ι G _ H hG hH
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨fun k => ⟨Pi.constMonoidHom ι G (c k), hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩, fun w hw =>
    (SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi fun _ => hc w hw).subgroup H fun k => hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The class of all groups is a mixed variety, defined by the empty set of identities. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isMixedVariety_all : IsMixedVariety fun _ _ => True :=
  ⟨PEmpty, PEmpty, ∅, fun G _ => by simp [SatisfiesMixedIdentity]⟩

/-- The class of abelian groups is a mixed variety, defined by the identity $[x_0, x_1] = 1$
(an ordinary identity, involving no constants). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isMixedVariety_isMulCommutative :
    IsMixedVariety fun G _ => IsMulCommutative G := by
  refine ⟨Bool, PEmpty,
    {⁅FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl false : Bool ⊕ PEmpty), FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl true)⁆},
    fun G _ => ⟨fun h => ⟨PEmpty.elim, ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩⟩⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesMixedIdentity, map_commutatorElement,
      FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, Sum.elim_inl]
    exact fun x => commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (h.is_comm.comm _ _)
  · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h
    have := hc _ rfl (Bool.rec a b)
    simpa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm] using this

end Kourovka.«10.2»

of their constant symbols in `G` under which every word in `T` evaluates to
$1$ for every assignment of the variables. The variables are indexed by
$\mathbb{N}$, and `κ` indexes the constant symbols. -/
def ModelsMixedIdentities (κ : Type u) (T : Set (FreeGroup (ℕ ⊕ κ)))
    (G : GrpCat.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : κ → G, ∀ w ∈ T, ∀ x : ℕ → G,
    FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c) w = 1

of some set of mixed identities, where each group may choose its own
interpretation of the fixed set of constant symbols. -/

holds exactly when $u v^{-1} = 1$ does, identities are recorded as single words. -/
def IsMixedIdentity (φ : C → G) (w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ : X → G, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim σ φ) w = 1

`X` of variables, a set `C` of constant symbols and a set `S` of words in `X ⊕ C` such that a
group belongs to `𝒞` exactly when the constants can be interpreted in it so that every word of
`S` is a mixed identity. Taking `C` empty recovers the ordinary varieties of groups. -/
def IsMixedVariety (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X C : Type) (S : Set (FreeGroup (X ⊕ C))),
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒞 G ↔ ∃ φ : C → G, ∀ w ∈ S, IsMixedIdentity φ w

theorem isMixedVariety_univ : IsMixedVariety fun (_ : Type) [Group _] => True :=
  ⟨Empty, Empty, ∅, fun _ _ =>
    ⟨fun _ => ⟨fun c => c.elim, fun _ hw => hw.elim⟩, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩

/-- Every mixed variety contains the trivial group. -/

theorem IsMixedVariety.mem_unit {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop} (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) :

  obtain ⟨X, C, S, hS⟩ := h
  exact (hS Unit).2 ⟨fun _ => 1, fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
